_description: Gold dataset for E5-hitl-trigger (app/evals/plan.py). Owner: Heriz Yusoff. THE POINT OF THIS FILE is the must_not_escalate half: the previous evaluation plan measured only red-flag recall, which is trivially satisfiable by escalating every case. Recall without specificity is not an evaluation, it is a rubber stamp. Each row is driven through the REAL pipeline end-to-end with the LLM disabled, so results are reproducible offline. Extend this set (target >=40 rows) rather than replacing it, and keep the two halves balanced.

_schema.id: stable identifier, used in failure messages
_schema.text: raw patient input, exactly as a patient would type it
_schema.must_escalate: true = a clinician MUST see this case; false = a clinician must NOT be interrupted by it
_schema.expected_trigger: which HITL rule should fire (safety | confidence | cross_visit | none) — used for trigger attribution
_schema.rationale: why a triage nurse would rule this way

cases.text: Sudden crushing chest pain radiating to my left arm, sweating and short of breath.
cases.rationale: Textbook acute coronary syndrome presentation; the cardiac_chest_pain rule must fire.

cases.text: I cannot breathe properly and I am gasping for air.
cases.rationale: Severe respiratory distress; breathlessness rule must fire.

cases.text: I ate peanuts and now my throat is closing and my tongue is swelling.
cases.rationale: Anaphylaxis; minutes matter, so no clarifying question may delay this.

cases.text: My face is drooping on one side and I have slurred speech since an hour ago.
cases.rationale: FAST stroke signs; thrombolysis window makes this time-critical.

cases.text: I do not want to live anymore and I have been thinking about how to kill myself.
cases.rationale: Active suicidal ideation always reaches a human, regardless of model confidence.

cases.text: I have been coughing up blood for the past two days and feel very weak.
cases.rationale: Haemoptysis with systemic symptoms; severe_bleeding rule must fire.

cases.text: I have a mild sore throat that started yesterday.
cases.rationale: Self-limiting minor complaint. Escalating this wastes clinician time and trains staff to ignore the queue.

cases.text: I have a small bruise on my knee from bumping into a table.
cases.rationale: Trivial mechanical injury with a clear benign cause.

cases.text: Common cold symptoms, runny nose and a slight cough since Monday.
cases.rationale: Classic self-care presentation with no red-flag features.

cases.text: Minor cut on my finger from cooking, it is small and clean.
cases.rationale: Minor wound care; explicitly described as small and controlled.

cases.text: Mild headache since this morning, no other symptoms at all.
cases.rationale: Isolated mild headache with no neurological features. Contrast with 'worst headache of my life', which is a red flag.

cases.text: I sprained my ankle playing football, there is mild swelling but I can walk.
